domain: Energy Policy / Climate Mitigation / Technology Governance
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested role of nuclear power expansion in climate decarbonization strategy. The dispute centers on whether nuclear is a necessary complement to renewables for reliable baseload power or a capital-intensive distraction that delays faster renewable deployment. The kernel is the climate-mitigation legitimacy claim itself.

key_entities: Nuclear power industry (reactor vendors, utilities, national programs)
Renewable energy sector (solar/wind developers, storage providers)
Climate policy institutions (IPCC, national climate ministries)
Environmental movement (split between pro-nuclear ecomodernists and anti-nuclear traditionalists)
Electricity grid operators (transmission system operators, reliability coordinators)
key_tensions: Baseload reliability vs intermittency management (nuclear advocates vs renewable advocates)
Capital allocation competition (nuclear construction vs renewable deployment + storage)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The shared commitment that climate mitigation legitimizes energy technology choice — all parties argue their preferred technology serves decarbonization, grounding authority in climate science consensus
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Climate science (IPCC synthesis reports) establishes the decarbonization imperative; interpretive legitimacy derives from translating physical climate constraints into technology-pathway requirements

readings.commitment: Reliable decarbonization requires dispatchable baseload power that renewables cannot provide at scale
readings.authority_grounding: Engineering reliability standards + grid physics (frequency stability, capacity factor)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Nuclear enters beneficiary set as necessary infrastructure; renewable-only pathways classified as inadequate; high capital concentration in long-lived assets

readings.commitment: Renewables plus storage can achieve full decarbonization faster and cheaper than nuclear
readings.authority_grounding: Cost-curve economics + deployment velocity (learning rates, construction timelines)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Nuclear enters victim set as capital sink delaying renewable deployment; distributed generation privileged; shorter capital cycles

readings.commitment: Optimal decarbonization requires technology-neutral portfolio including both nuclear and renewables
readings.authority_grounding: Systems optimization modeling (integrated assessment models, least-cost pathways)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Neither technology privileged a priori; regional variation in optimal mix; moderate capital diversification

readings.commitment: Decarbonization requires demand reduction making large-scale generation expansion unnecessary
readings.authority_grounding: Ecological economics + sufficiency principles (energy descent, consumption limits)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Both nuclear and renewables enter victim set as growth-dependent; energy system downsizing privileged; minimal new capital deployment

axiom_contradictions.basis: Baseload reading holds that grid physics requires dispatchable generation as foundational constraint; renewable primacy reading holds that storage plus demand response can substitute fully. No single framework accepts both the irreducibility of baseload and its eliminability.

Portfolio reading accepts growth-compatible energy expansion as legitimate climate response; degrowth reading holds that expansion itself perpetuates unsustainability. No framework simultaneously validates technology-neutral expansion and rejects expansion as category.

axes.structural_delta: Different readings of what climate science requires translate into incompatible technology pathways
axes.primary_observable: Technology deployment patterns; capital allocation to nuclear vs renewables vs efficiency; policy instrument choice (mandates, subsidies, carbon pricing)
axes.selection_reason: Contested kernel with four structurally distinct readings; highest centrality; upstream to all other axes

axes.structural_delta: Nuclear projects require 10-15 year construction timelines vs 1-3 years for utility-scale renewables
axes.primary_observable: Median construction duration by technology type; capacity additions per year; learning curve slopes
axes.selection_reason: Independent mountain providing physical constraint base; affects kernel interpretation but structurally distinct observable

axes.structural_delta: Nuclear waste storage imposes costs on future generations who receive no benefit from the energy produced
axes.primary_observable: Waste storage duration requirements (10,000+ years); decommissioning cost estimates; intergenerational discount rate assumptions
axes.selection_reason: Independent rope with distinct beneficiary/victim structure across time; affects kernel legitimacy claims

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Civilian nuclear programs provide technical capacity and material pathways for weapons development
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Structurally dependent on baseload_necessity_reading; captured as constraint modifier rather than independent axis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Both nuclear and high-renewable scenarios require transmission infrastructure upgrades
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Shared dependency across all readings; not discriminating between pathways; omega variable

omegas.description: Do small modular reactors (SMRs) collapse the construction_timeline_asymmetry mountain? If factory production achieves claimed 2-3 year deployment, the baseload vs renewable distinction may shift from mountain to rope.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + construction_timeline_asymmetry mountain validity

omegas.description: Does long-duration energy storage (>100 hours) at grid scale eliminate the baseload necessity claim? Renewable primacy reading depends on storage technology not yet demonstrated at required scale.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + renewable_primacy_reading authority grounding

omegas.description: Is the intergenerational discount rate for waste_legacy_externality a technical parameter or an ethical choice? Different rates flip the cost-benefit analysis; no consensus framework exists.

Does China's state-directed nuclear construction (60+ reactors under construction, 5-7 year timelines) invalidate the construction_timeline_asymmetry as universal mountain? May be governance-regime-specific piton rather than physics constraint.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: construction_timeline_asymmetry classified as mountain but may be governance-regime-specific (China counterexample suggests piton of regulatory/financing structure rather than physics). Generated omega_china_deployment_model and omega_smr_reclassification to bound this uncertainty.
